title: Article 222 — Transfer of a Judge from one High Court to another

content.overview: Article 222 provides that the President may, after consultation with the Chief Justice of India, transfer a Judge from one High Court to any other High Court. When a Judge is so transferred, he is entitled to such compensatory allowance as Parliament may by law determine (and until so determined, as prescribed by Presidential order).
content.glance: President may transfer HC Judge to another HC after consultation with CJI. Compensatory allowance as determined by law.
content.study:
Article 222 transfer power:
- President may transfer a Judge from one High Court to another after consultation with the Chief Justice of India.
- Compensatory allowance for the transferred Judge as Parliament by law determines.

Transfer practice is subject to the collegium/consultation framework developed by the Supreme Court.

Examination: President + CJI consultation; compensatory allowance; any other High Court.

sections.heading: Key rules
sections.body:
1. President may transfer a Judge from one HC to another after consultation with the CJI.
2. Transferred Judge entitled to compensatory allowance as determined by parliamentary law (or Presidential order until then).

questionsAndAnswers.question: Can a High Court Judge be transferred?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Yes. Under Article 222, the President may, after consultation with the Chief Justice of India, transfer a Judge from one High Court to any other High Court. The transferred Judge is entitled to such compensatory allowance as Parliament may by law determine.

examTips: Transfer by President after CJI consultation; compensatory allowance.

keyTakeaways: Art 222: transfer of HC Judges with CJI consultation.
